message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on a jewelry storage system made of plastic. The candidate headings are 3924 (household articles of plastics), 3926 (other articles of plastics), 4202 (jewelry boxes and cases), and 9403 (furniture).

Heading 4202 covers "jewelry boxes" with an outer surface of plastic sheeting, but the ruling would likely treat this item as a stand-alone cabinet-like unit. Furniture under 9403 is also possible, but a 12x8x24 inch item that sits on a dresser or hangs on a wall is more like a jewelry box or armoire. Heading 4202.99 covers "other" containers, and 4202.92 covers containers with an outer surface of plastic sheeting or textile materials. For jewelry boxes, 4202.91 and 4202.99 cover "other" items, with 4202.99.90 as the residual.

Heading 4202 jewelry boxes are described as "jewelry boxes" in the sense of fitted cases. A molded plastic and acrylic organizer probably falls under 3924.90.56 (other household articles of plastics) or 3926.90.99. However, 4202 includes jewelry boxes of any material, and Note 3 to Chapter 39 and the Chapter 42 notes do not exclude it. Jewelry boxes are specifically named in 4202., with subheading 4202.92.45 or 4202.99.90.

Because the item is a stand-alone modular jewelry storage system with drawers and a door, a furniture-like cabinet is plausible, but 9403 covers furniture that is floor-standing or wall-hung only if it is large. Small tabletop jewelry organizers have often been classified in 4202.

I'll choose 4202.92.9026 ("other" containers with outer surface of plastic sheeting). Because the item is molded plastic and acrylic rather than plastic sheeting, 4202.99.9000 is the better fit.

{"hts_code": "4202.99.9000", "reason": "A fitted jewelry storage case/box of plastic and acrylic is a jewelry box, classified in heading 4202 under the residual 'other' subheading."}
